# ADO403: hardcoded-secret

A secret-looking variable has a literal value.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Category** | Best practices |
| **Default severity** | warning |
| **Enabled by default** | yes |
| **Checked on** | the template-expanded pipeline (positions point at the original files) |

## Description

Variables and step environment variables whose names suggest secrets (password, token, apiKey, ...) shouldn't have literal values in YAML. Use secret variables, variable groups or Azure Key Vault. Connection strings without a credential key (password, accountKey, sharedAccessKey, ...), such as managed-identity strings like RunAs=App;AppId=..., aren't reported.

## Example

Problem:

```yaml
variables:
  apiToken: 3f9a8c...
```

Instead:

```yaml
variables:
- group: my-secrets # defines apiToken as a secret
```

## Configuration

Change the severity or turn the rule off in `.adolint.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  ADO403: off   # off | info | warning | error
```

Or on the command line: `adolint lint --disable ADO403` or `--enable ADO403`.

Suppress a single finding with a comment on the line before it (or `disable-line` at the end of the line):

```yaml
# adolint:disable-next-line ADO403
```

Questions about ADO403, or a false positive? [Open an issue](https://github.com/danielsada/go-ado-pipelines-lint/issues/new?title=ADO403%3A+) with the YAML that triggered it.
